observation_summary: The cumulativeProbability method in NormalDistributionImpl throws a ConvergenceException when input values are extreme (e.g., Infinity), because the underlying Erf calculation fails to converge. The existing code only caught MaxIterationsExceededException, failing to handle other convergence-related exceptions.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a guard condition (if (FastMath.abs(dev) > 40 * standardDeviation)) to validate the input range before proceeding with the calculation. This prevents the algorithm from attempting to compute values that are known to be outside the convergence range, effectively acting as a boundary check. This is a classic 'Checking' defect where a missing validation guard causes an exception.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of a try-catch block and the addition of an if-statement to check the range of 'dev'.
The bug report explicitly suggests catching all convergence exceptions for very large/small values.
The stack trace shows a ConvergenceException occurring during the calculation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes the execution flow, the root cause is the lack of a boundary check for extreme inputs, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
